pr_body:
Many consumers of the field caps API need to do some post-processing of the
results before they can use them; for instance, Kibana would like to exclude
multifields from certain field selections, or would like to display only `geo_point`
fields in Maps. ML and QL consumers exclude nested fields in certain 
circumstances.  This post-processing is possible at the moment, but can be
hacky; and in all cases it involves sending the whole (possibly very large) field
caps response over the wire and then whittling it down in the client. It is also not
guaranteed to be accurate - runtime fields may be incorrectly classified as multifields,
for example.

This commit pushes filtering into elasticsearch itself, reducing the amount of data
that needs to be transported and ensuring better accuracy.  The field caps API gets
two new parameters:
* `filters` - a comma-delimited list that may contain any combination of: `+metadata`, 
  `-metadata`, `-nested`, `-parent`, `-multifield`
* `types` - a comma-delimited list of field types; only fields that have a type in this set
  will be returned

The API will make best-effort attempts to apply the filters post-hoc to responses from
older nodes, so this should still work in a mixed-cluster or cross-cluster situation.

Fixes #82966, #72174

issue_context.title: Add extra filters to field caps
issue_context.body:
A number of clients of field caps want to exclude or filter down to a specific subset of fields that are defined by mapping parameters.  For example, Kibana Discover presents users with a list of fields that excludes multifields; ML dataframes and QL want to filter out nested fields; TSDB wants to load only fields marked as dimensions.  We have various heuristics to guide clients on how to identify these type of fields, but it would be a lot simpler in many cases to identify them within ES itself and filter them out on the server side.  It would also reduce the number of bytes sent over the wire.

Looking through internal usages I can see four filters that we could add to start with: `metadata`, `multifield`, `nested`, `dimension`.  Each could be prefixed with a `+` or `-` to indicate an inclusive or exclusive filter.

Adding filters to data nodes should be simple.  These four filters can also be implemented in a best-effort fashion on a co-ordinating node for mixed-cluster or cross-cluster cases where the data node does not have the filter implemented.
comments:
Related: it would be great if we could filter by type as well: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/72174

As @romseygeek mentions, searching for fields based on their capabilities, is really useful to bootstrap a UX,

Another example of more advanced filtering: the ability to determine whether fields are sparsely populated or not: https://github.com/elastic/kibana/issues/100779 (this proposes to add this logic into Kibana, but Elasticsearch could support this as well for more broader applicability)

I'm wondering if this could be extended even further to include filtering based on partial matches for the field-name, aka "auto-suggest": https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/74816

We can already match on partial field names in field caps. I think the reason that we were discussion a separate 'field completion' API was that field caps are built entirely from mappings, and so can't introspect into flattened fields.

I don't see this one documented: is it `+parent` or just `parent`?

This is just plain `parent` and acts as the equivalent of a `SHOULD` clause - in other words, do return parent information.  Clients that aren't filtering out nested or multifield entries still use this to do their own checks, but once they start using filters they can filter out parents instead.  At some point in the future I envisage that we will filter out parents by default, and then clients will have to explicitly include `parent` if they still want that information.
